subject: P value and adjusted p value 0

messages.author: 395fec07c2012bfa
messages.subject: P value and adjusted p value 0
parts:
Hi MSStats team,

This has been discussed before but could you please explain again?

I found around 80 proteins with p and adjusted p value as '0' in a matrix of 6000 proteins. 
Some of them are 'one condition missing' but others with strong changes in the logFC column. Can we take them as significant? I am wondering how a volcano plot can be created with these proteins included! 

I have updated the top 100 protein (sorted on adjusted P) list with group comparison + summarized data/protein to have a look. 

best regards,
Sudip

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: P value and adjusted p value 0
parts:
Hi Sudip,

The proteins with a pvalue of 0, log FC of infinity, and say "one condition missing", cannot be modeled because we have no measurements for one of the conditions in the comparison. We will not impute these missing values as we have no evidence of where the missing values should be.

For the remaining ones, I think the pvalues are not 0, but are very small and excel is rounding them to 0 because it cannot handle how small they are. You'll see the proteins at the bottom of your list are not actually 0 but very small. I would assume the others have an even lower pvalue and excel just can't show them. 

Best,
Devon
